config.title: Error Handling & Debugging

intro.title: Error Handling & Debugging
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple calculator app that handles common input errors, like division by zero or invalid numbers. You'll learn the core concepts of error handling and debugging using try...catch blocks and console logging. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's built-in Error object and browser developer tools. By the end, you'll be able to write code that gracefully manages errors and uses debugging techniques to fix issues.
intro.usecase: Error handling is essential in any application that interacts with users or external systems. In forms, proper validation prevents invalid submissions and guides users with clear error messages. Dashboard applications use error boundaries to gracefully handle data fetch failures while keeping the UI functional. API integrations implement try-catch blocks to manage network issues and provide fallback content when services are unavailable.

objectives: Implement try-catch blocks to handle runtime errors in JavaScript functions
Apply console.log() and console.error() statements to trace program execution
Construct custom error objects with descriptive messages for specific failure cases
Configure error boundaries to prevent application crashes from uncaught exceptions
Manipulate the call stack information to identify the source of bugs
Initialize error handling for asynchronous operations using promises and async/await
Integrate debugging tools like breakpoints and step-through execution in browser developer tools

steps.title: Import console and error handling utilities
steps.instruction: At the top of your JavaScript file, import the console object and error handling utilities that will be used throughout this lesson. Write: `import console from 'console';` and `import { Error, TypeError, tryCatch } from 'error-handling';`
steps.hint: Start with the import keyword followed by what you want to import and the module name in quotes. You can write multiple import statements on separate lines.
steps.seedCode:
// No code yet — this is the first step.
// Add your import statements here:
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have import statements for console and error handling utilities, making them available for use in the lesson.
successCriteria: Console is imported from 'console', and Error, TypeError, and tryCatch are imported from 'error-handling'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the console and error handling utilities needed for this lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some utilities, but check that you have all required imports: console from 'console', and Error, TypeError, and tryCatch from 'error-handling'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Make sure to write import statements for console and the error handling utilities as specified.

steps.title: Create main error handling function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'handleErrors' that will contain all error handling examples. Make it return null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to include the function body with a return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleErrors is defined with a body that returns null.
successCriteria: The handleErrors function is created with the correct name and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main error handling function structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named 'handleErrors' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the name 'handleErrors' and included a return statement.

steps.title: Initialize error tracking variables
steps.instruction: Inside your handleErrors function, declare three variables: errorMessage, errorType, and debugLogs. Initialize them with empty strings or arrays as appropriate for storing error data.
steps.hint: You can use let or const to declare variables. For example: let errorMessage = ''; const debugLogs = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: Your handleErrors function will have three variables declared and initialized to store error information.
successCriteria: The handleErrors function contains three variables: errorMessage, errorType, and debugLogs, each properly initialized.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the variables needed to track error messages, types, and debugging logs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared all three required variables: errorMessage, errorType, and debugLogs.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the handleErrors function, declare three variables to store error data: errorMessage, errorType, and debugLogs.

steps.title: Create basic try-catch structure
steps.instruction: Inside your handleErrors function, add a try-catch block structure with empty try and catch blocks.
steps.hint: Use the try keyword followed by curly braces for the try block, then the catch keyword with parentheses for the error parameter and curly braces for the catch block.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your handleErrors function will have a basic try-catch structure ready for error handling logic.
successCriteria: The handleErrors function contains a try block and a catch block with an error parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the basic try-catch structure to your error handling function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both try and catch blocks with proper syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The try-catch structure is missing or incorrect. Remember to include both try and catch blocks with curly braces.

steps.title: Add console.log for debugging
steps.instruction: Inside your handleErrors function, add a console.log statement before the try-catch block to log a message indicating the function has started executing.
steps.hint: Place console.log('Starting error handling...') right before the try keyword.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleErrors function will log a message to the console when it starts executing, helping you trace program flow.
successCriteria: A console.log statement is added inside the handleErrors function before the try-catch block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a console.log statement to help debug your function execution.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added console.log inside the handleErrors function before the try-catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding console.log('Starting error handling...') inside the handleErrors function before the try-catch block.

steps.title: Implement error throwing
steps.instruction: Inside the try block of your handleErrors function, add a throw statement that creates a new Error with the message 'Intentional error for demonstration'.
steps.hint: Use the throw keyword followed by new Error('your message') to intentionally create an error.
steps.analogousExample:
// Throwing a custom error
throw new Error('Something went wrong!');
steps.expectedOutcome: The try block now contains a throw statement that will intentionally create an error when the function runs.
successCriteria: The handleErrors function includes a throw statement with new Error('Intentional error for demonstration') inside the try block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an intentional error throw. This demonstrates how to create custom errors in JavaScript.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the throw keyword followed by new Error() with the exact message 'Intentional error for demonstration'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The try block should contain a throw statement that creates a new Error with the specified message. Review the syntax for throwing errors.

steps.title: Add error catching and logging
steps.instruction: Inside the catch block of your handleErrors function, add a console.log statement to log the error details.
steps.hint: The catch block receives an error object. Use console.log to output it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The catch block will log error details to the console when an error occurs.
successCriteria: The catch block contains a console.log statement that logs the error object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error logging to the catch block. This will help you see what went wrong when debugging.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're logging the error object inside the catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The catch block should contain a console.log statement to log the error details. Try adding console.log(error) or similar.

steps.title: Wire error display to error state
steps.instruction: Inside the handleErrors function, update the return statement to display the error message from the error tracking variable instead of the placeholder text.
steps.hint: Replace the placeholder text in the return statement with the variable that holds the error message.

steps.title: Add error triggering controls
steps.instruction: Inside the handleErrors function, add a button element that triggers an error when clicked by calling a function that throws an error.
steps.hint: Create a button with an onClick handler that calls a function containing a throw statement.
